paper_name: Temporally Consistent Unbalanced Optimal Transport for Unsupervised Action Segmentation

sections.abstract: The paper introduces Action Segmentation Optimal Transport (ASOT), a novel approach for action segmentation in long, untrimmed videos. ASOT addresses the challenge of decoding temporally consistent segmentations from noisy affinity matrices by solving a fused, unbalanced Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) optimal transport problem. Unlike previous methods, ASOT does not require prior knowledge of action ordering to maintain temporal consistency. The method is efficient, solvable on GPUs using projected mirror descent, and achieves state-of-the-art results in unsupervised learning settings on the Breakfast, 50-Salads, YouTube Instructions, and Desktop Assembly datasets.
sections.introduction: Action segmentation requires understanding long, untrimmed videos where individual actions occupy temporal blocks of frames, a property known as "temporal consistency." Existing unsupervised methods often rely on post-processing with Hidden Markov Models (HMMs), which require knowing the action order beforehand, or balanced optimal transport (OT), which incorrectly assumes uniform action distributions. ASOT is proposed to overcome these limitations by encoding temporal consistency into a fused, unbalanced Gromov-Wasserstein problem that handles order variations and long-tailed class distributions without requiring known action sequences.
sections.method: ASOT formulates action segmentation as an OT problem where the coupling $$\mathbf{T} \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times K}$$ represents soft assignments between $N$ frames and $K$ actions. It builds on foundations of Kantorovich OT (KOT): $$\min_{\mathbf{T} \in \mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{p}, \mathbf{q}}} \mathcal{F}_{\text{KOT}}(\mathbf{C}^k, \mathbf{T}) \coloneqq \langle \mathbf{C}^k, \mathbf{T} \rangle$$ (Eq. 1), Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) OT: $$\mathcal{F}_{\text{GW}}(\mathbf{C}^v, \mathbf{C}^a, \mathbf{T}) \coloneqq \sum_{i,k \in [n], j,l \in [m]} L(C_{ik}^v, C_{jl}^a) T_{ij}T_{kl}$$ (Eq. 2), and Fused GW (FGW): $$\mathcal{F}_{\text{FGW}}(\mathbf{C}, \mathbf{T}) \coloneqq \alpha \mathcal{F}_{\text{GW}}(\mathbf{C}^v, \mathbf{C}^a, \mathbf{T}) + (1-\alpha) \mathcal{F}_{\text{KOT}}(\mathbf{C}^k, \mathbf{T})$$ (Eq. 3). It addresses long-tailed distributions via Unbalanced OT: $$\min_{\mathbf{T} \in \mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{p}}} \mathcal{F}_{\text{FGW}}(\mathbf{C}, \mathbf{T}) + \lambda \text{D}_{\text{KL}}(\mathbf{T}^\top \mathbf{1}_n \| \mathbf{q})$$ (Eq. 4). Temporal consistency is enforced via structural priors: $$\mathbf{C}^v_{ik} \coloneqq 1/r$$ if $$1 \leq |i - k| \leq Nr$$ and 0 otherwise, and $$\mathbf{C}^a_{jl} \coloneqq 0$$ if $$j = l$$ and 1 otherwise (Eq. 5). The unsupervised pipeline generates pseudo-labels $$\mathbf{T}$$ to train an encoder $$\mathbf{X}^b := f_\theta(\mathcal{V}^b)$$ by minimizing $$\mathcal{L}_{\text{train}}(\theta) = -\frac{1}{B}\sum_{b=1}^B \sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{j=1}^k T^b_{ij} \log P^b_{ij}$$ (Eq. 7), where similarities are $$P^b_{ij} \coloneqq \frac{\exp (\mathbf{X}^b \mathbf{A}^\top / \tau )_{ij}}{\sum _l\exp (\mathbf{X}^b \mathbf{A}^\top / \tau )_{il}}$$ (Eq. 6). A global temporal prior $$\hat{\mathbf{C}}^k = \mathbf{C}^k + \rho \mathbf{R}$$ with $$R_{ij} = |i/N - j/K|$$ is used during training.
sections.experiments: The encoder is an MLP with one hidden layer (128 units, ReLU), trained using the Adam optimizer (LR $10^{-3}$, weight decay $10^{-4}$). Datasets include Breakfast (1700 videos, 48 actions), YouTube Instructions (150 videos), 50 Salads (50 videos), and Desktop Assembly (76 videos). Evaluation metrics are Mean over-frames (MoF), F1-score, and mean intersection-over-union (mIoU). Hungarian matching maps learned clusters to ground truth actions for both per-video (Unsup. per) and dataset-wide (Unsup. full) evaluation.
